literal: If the wide-staring eye, when a spear is taken to be thrown, yields and blinks, is that not a defeat to the brave warriors?
translation: If a warrior blinks his wide-staring eyes when an enemy hurls a spear at him, is that momentary blink not a retreat and defeat for his valor?
modern: பகைவன் தன் மேல் வேலை வீசி எறியும்போது, அவனை உற்று நோக்கிய கண்கள் அஞ்சி இமைக்குமானால், அதுவே அந்த வீரனுக்குப் தோல்வி அல்லவா?
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate standard of military pride and valor. A true warrior keeps his eyes wide open, staring defiantly at the enemy. If he blinks (இமைப்பின்) even for a split second when a spear is thrown at him, that reflex is considered a defeat (ஒட்டு) to his heroic spirit. The word 'அழித்து' here refers to breaking or yielding the steady, fearless gaze of the eye. To the truly brave, even a natural physical reflex of self-defense is seen as a shameful retreat.
